note: The tires of World: the codes of ETRTO and of ISO 4000-1 (cars and vans), ISO 5751 (motorcycles) and ISO 5775 (bicycles). The size of a tire from its code: the section height is the section width times the aspect ratio; the outer diameter is the rim diameter and two section heights (ISO 4000-1:2021, clause 6). A tire of a data sheet has its own sizes and mass.

rim.source: ISO 4000-1:2001/Amd 1:2004, Table 1: the nominal rim diameter of each code (mm).

load.source: The load index: the load of one tire (kg). 60 to 120: Tyreleader, Car tyres: load and speed indexes; 121 to 130: Kramp, Technische Daten: Load Index / Speed Index (the same values as PureTyre).

speed.source: The speed symbol: the most speed of a tire (km/h): Tyreleader and Kramp (the same values).

datasheet.source: The tires of the makers: the measuring rim (in), the section width (mm), the outer diameter (mm) and the mass (kg). 235/65R16C 121/119R, LT245/75R16 120/116R and LT225/75R16 115/112R: Michelin, Agilis CrossClimate data book, pages 116 and 117 (the masses: tiresize.com); 215/50R17 91H: Michelin Energy Saver A/S (tiresize.com); 80/90-14, 90/90-14, 90/90-21 and 120/90-17: Mitas, Product catalog 2020, pages 10 and 24 (the design sizes; no mass); 37-622: Schwalbe, Marathon GreenGuard (730 g; the diameter of ISO 5775: 622 + 2 x 37 mm).
